items.title: John Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: I work with because he’s with Joe and anything I can do to work with him is fine... I have a contract, a Nancy Wilson contract that has 40 pages on it, for Columbia Records.

ctx.x: And that was it. No contract. No nothing. And the other people I guess came along through the record companies. In those days, especially Capitol Records, almost anybody who was anybody that came through the label that didn’t have management I’d get a call and they’d say — in jazz that is, you know — “do you want to manage this person?” Or they’d recommend me, you know. And that way I remember Dakota Staton was one. She was on Capitol Records and Dave Cavanaugh, who was the A&R man for George Shearing and later…
Somebody take the phone out of your hands—

items.title: Nancy Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995
items.q: So the object of my strategy was, if I’m going to do this, the only person who I would trust to help and be there for me would be John Levy.

ctx.x: He, there’s been a few people in your career that in the beginning were instrumental I think, and he was one and John Levy.
But before John Levy, and before Cannonball, there was a band called The Rusty Bryant band who recorded for Dot. And I understand there is a copy of a bootleg, because I © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

never signed with Dot. There is supposed to be a record out of me, somewhere, on Dot. And I do believe that was with Rusty Bryant’s band. And before Rusty Bryant, because I didn’t join that band until after high school, there was a band called Sir Raleigh Randolph and his Sultans of Swing. I was fifteen, and the band’s singer. And I played all the cabarets with — in the midwest and in Ohio. I felt really blessed to do that. It was unbelievable to be able to sing all those wonderful songs at a young, very young…

items.title: John Levy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Cannonball, and Nancy pretty well through – just one period when her husband got involved and we had to split up for a period of time, about a year, during her career.

ctx.x: Do you go back because of the hurricane?

No. I went back – Nancy Wilson did a benefit concert for the university there, and we went back for that affair. That’s when I – the most recent time that I went back. Note: Nancy’s performance was for Dillard University, June 30, 2006
You go by the house whenever you visit?
